questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Annual rings are used to calculate the age of tree.
Reason : Secondary growth is not found in bamboo.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Each year the tree forms new cells (secondary growth) arranged in concentric circles called annual rings. These rings show amount of wood produced during one growing season. By counting the annual rings, the age of a tree can be determined. This phenomenon is called dendrochronology. Only plants showing secondary growth show annual rings. Bamboo is a monocot and hence secondary growth is absent in bamboo.

options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

questions.solution: Archaea superficially resemble bacteria in terms of size and cellular organisation. However, they are surprisingly similar to eukaryotes at the molecular level. For instance all Archaea replicate their DNA and synthesise proteins using molecular machines like those of eukaryotes. In Archaea and eukaryotes, larger genomes contain a greater proportion of intergenic material and genome size appears to correlate negatively with the strength of selection.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What happens to a cell during M phase of cell cycle?
questions.solution: During $G_1$ phase, the cell is in resting state and the nucleocytoplasmic index is stable. During the $\mathrm{S}$ phase of the cell cycle, DNA replicates, consequently nucleocytoplasmic index increases due to increase in nuclear volume. During $G_2$ phase, the cell is again stable. During M phase, nucleocytoplasmic index decreases. After $M$ phase or mitosis when the cell divides, nucleoplasmic index returns to normal.

What is the activation energy $(\mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{mol})$ for a reaction if its rate constant doubles when the temperature is raised from $300 \mathrm{~K}$ to $400 \mathrm{~K}$ ?
$\left(R=8.314 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}\right)$

questions.q: Calculate molarity of $63 \% \mathrm{w} / \mathrm{w} \mathrm{HNO}_3$ solution if density is $1.4 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mL}$.
questions.solution:
$63 \%$ nitric acid by mass means that mass of nitric acid $=63 \mathrm{~g}$
Mass of solution $=100 \mathrm{~g}$
Molar mass of $\mathrm{HNO}_3=63 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
Mole of $\mathrm{HNO}_3=\frac{63 \mathrm{~g}}{63 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}}=1 \mathrm{~mole}$
Density of solution $=1.4 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mL}^{-1}\therefore \quad$ Volume of solution
$=\frac{100 \mathrm{~g}}{1.4 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mL}^{-1}}=71.428 \mathrm{~mL}=0.071428 \mathrm{~L}$
Molarity of solution $=\frac{\text { Moles of solute }}{\text { Volume of solution in } \mathrm{L}}=\frac{1.0}{0.071428} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}=14 \mathrm{M}$

questions.q: If maximum energy is stored in capacitor at $t=0$, then find the time after which current in the circuit will be maximum
questions.solution:
In $L-C$ oscillations, total time in one complete cycle is, $T=2 \pi \sqrt{L C}\begin{aligned} & T=2 \pi \sqrt{25 \times 10^{-3} \times 10 \times 10^{-6}} \\ & \Rightarrow T=2 \pi \sqrt{25 \times 10^{-8}} \\ & =\pi \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{sec}\end{aligned}$
After time $T / 4$ capacitor is fully discharged and current in circuit will be maximum, then $\frac{T}{4}=\frac{\pi \times 10^{-3}}{4}=\frac{\pi}{4} \mathrm{~ms}$

questions.q: For a toroid $N=500$, radius $=40 \mathrm{~cm}$, and area of cross section $=10 \mathrm{~cm}^2$. Find inductance.
questions.solution: If we flow a current $i$, then $\begin{aligned} & \phi_{\text {self }}=(B \times A) \times N=\left(\frac{\mu_0 N i}{2 \pi R}\right) A \times N \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \phi_{\text {self }}=\left(\frac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{2 \pi R}\right) i \text { and } \phi_{\text {self }}=L i\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & L=\frac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{2 \pi R}=\frac{\mu_0}{4 \pi} \frac{2 N^2 A}{R} \\ & \Rightarrow L=\left(10^{-7}\right) \times \frac{2 \times(500)^2 \times 10 \times\left(10^{-2}\right)^2}{0.4} \\ &=125 \mu \mathrm{H}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform coil of self-inductance $1.8 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{H}$ and resistance $6 \Omega$ is broken up into two identical coils. These two coils are then connected in parallel across a $12 \mathrm{~V}$ battery. The circuit time constant and steady state current through the battery respectively are
questions.solution:
When coil is broken into two identical parts, then resistance of each part
$R^{\prime}=\frac{R}{2}=\frac{6}{2}=3 \Omega$
Inductance of each part
$L^{\prime}=\frac{L}{2}=\frac{1.8}{2} \times 10^{-4}=0.9 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{H}$
Now, time constant $\tau=\frac{L^{\prime}}{R^{\prime}}\tau=\frac{L}{2 \times \frac{R}{2}}=\frac{L}{R}=\frac{1.8 \times 10^{-4}}{6}=30 \mu \mathrm{s}$
Now, effective resistance when both coils are connected in parallel
$R^{\prime \prime}=\frac{R^{\prime} \times R^{\prime}}{R^{\prime}+R^{\prime}}=\frac{3 \times 3}{3+3}=\frac{9}{6} \Omega$
So, maximum current drawn from battery
$I=\frac{V}{R^{\prime \prime}}=\frac{12}{9 / 6}=8 \mathrm{~A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A proton of velocity $(3 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}) \mathrm{m} \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ enters a field of magnetic induction $(2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k})$ tesla. The acceleration produced in the proton in $\mathrm{m} \mathrm{s}^{-2}$ is (Specific charge of proton $=0.96 \times 10^8 \mathrm{C} \mathrm{kg}^{-1}$ )
questions.solution:
Here, $\vec{v}=3 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j} \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}\vec{B}=2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k} \mathrm{~T}$
Specific charge of proton
$=\frac{e}{m}=0.96 \times 10^8 \mathrm{C} \mathrm{kg}^{-1}$
Force on a proton in a uniform magnetic field is
$\begin{aligned} & \vec{F}=e(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}) \\ & =e[(3 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}) \times(2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k})] \\ & =e(6 \hat{k}-9 \hat{j}+6 \hat{i})=e(6 \hat{i}-9 \hat{j}+6 \hat{k}) \mathrm{N}\end{aligned}$
Acceleration of the proton,
$\begin{aligned} & \vec{a}=\frac{\vec{F}}{m}=\frac{e(6 \hat{i}-9 \hat{j}+6 \hat{k})}{m} \\ & =0.96 \times 10^8(6 \hat{i}-9 \hat{j}+6 \hat{k}) \mathrm{m} \mathrm{s}^{-2} \\ & =2.88 \times 10^8(2 \hat{i}-3 \hat{j}+2 \hat{k}) \mathrm{m} \mathrm{s}^{-2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A projectile has a maximum range of $16 \mathrm{~km}$. At the highest point of its motion, it explodes into two equal masses. One mass drops vertically downwards. The horizontal distance covered by the other mass from the time of explosion is
questions.solution:
Maximum range,
$R_{\max }=\frac{u^2 \sin 2 \theta}{g}=\frac{u^2}{g}=16 \mathrm{~km}$
Range is maximum when $\theta=45^{\circ}$ Initial momentum at the highest point
$=m u \cos 45^{\circ}=\frac{m u}{\sqrt{2}}$
After explosion, the projectile breaks into two equal masses. As one mass drops vertically downwards, hence its velocity and momentum is zero in the $x$-direction.
Hence, if $v$ be the velocity of second mass, then according to law of conservation of momentum,
$m u \cos 45^{\circ}=\frac{m}{2} v \quad \therefore \quad v=2 u \cos 45^{\circ}$
Horizontal distance covered from the time of explosion
$\begin{aligned} & =v \times \frac{T}{2}=v \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2 u \sin 45^{\circ}}{g} \\ & =2 u \cos 45^{\circ} \times \frac{u \sin 45^{\circ}}{g} \\ & =\frac{u^2}{g} \times \sin 90^{\circ}=\frac{u^2}{g}=16 \mathrm{~km}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A bi-convex lens is formed with two thin plano-convex lenses as shown in the figure. Refractive index $n$ of the first lens is 1.5 and that of the second lens is 1.2. Both the curved surfaces are of the same radius of curvature $R=14 \mathrm{~cm}$. For this bi-convex lens, for an object distance of $40 \mathrm{~cm}$, the image distance will be
questions.solution:
According to lens maker's formula
$\frac{1}{f}=(n-1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)$
For the first lens : $n=1.5, R_1=+14 \mathrm{~cm}, R_2=\infty\therefore \quad \frac{1}{f_1}=(1.5-1)\left(\frac{1}{14}-\frac{1}{\infty}\right)=\frac{0.5}{14}$
For the second lens : $n=1.2, R_1=\infty, R_2=-14 \mathrm{~cm}\therefore \quad \frac{1}{f_2}=(1.2-1)\left(\frac{1}{\infty}-\frac{1}{-14}\right)=\frac{0.2}{14}$
The focal length of the bi-convex lens is
$\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{f_1}+\frac{1}{f_2}=\frac{0.5}{14}+\frac{0.2}{14}=\frac{0.7}{14}=\frac{1}{20}$
According to thin lens formula; $\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}\Rightarrow \frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{-40}=\frac{1}{20}$ or $v=40 \mathrm{~cm}$

Reason : $\frac{1}{f}=\left(\frac{\mu_g-\mu_a}{\mu_a}\right)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)$
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution:
As $\frac{1}{f}=\left(\frac{\mu_g}{\mu_a}-1\right)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)\frac{1}{10}=\left(\frac{3}{2}-1\right)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right) \Rightarrow\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)=\frac{1}{5}$
If $f_w$ is the focal length of the lens when immersed in water,
$\frac{1}{f_w}=\left(\frac{\mu_g}{\mu_w}-1\right)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)=\left(\frac{3 / 2}{4 / 3}-1\right)\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)=\frac{1}{40}$
Hence, $f_w=40 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block of mass $2 \mathrm{~kg} F(t) \uparrow$ is free to move along the $x$-axis. It is at rest and from $t=0$ onwards it is subjected to a timedependent force $F(t)$ in the $x$ direction. The force $F(t)$ varies with $t$ as shown in the figure. The kinetic energy of the block after 4.5 seconds is
questions.solution:
Change in momentum $=$ area under $F$ - $t$ graph
$\begin{aligned} \Delta p & =\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 3-\frac{1}{2} \times 1.5 \times \frac{4}{3} \times 1.5 \\ & {\left[\text { Force at } 4.5 \mathrm{~s}=\frac{4}{3} \times 1.5 \mathrm{~N}\right] } \\ & =6-1.5=4.5 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}\end{aligned}$
As $\Delta p=m(v-u)=m v \quad(\because u=0)\therefore \quad v=\frac{\Delta p}{m}=\frac{4.5 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}}{2 \mathrm{~kg}}=\frac{4.5}{2} \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$
Kinetic energy of the block after $4.5 \mathrm{~s}$ is
$K=\frac{1}{2} m v^2=\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \mathrm{~kg} \times\left(\frac{4.5}{2} \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}\right)^2=5.06 \mathrm{~J}$

questions.solution: Type I diabetes is an autoimmune disease wherein immune system destroys cells in pancreas called beta cells which make insulin. Insulin is a hormone that helps move sugar from blood into body tissues where cells use it as fuel. Damage to beta cells leads to build up of sugar in blood as cell are not able to utilise it which leads to high blood sugar. Assertion : Insulin forms hormone receptor complex which regulates the formation of second messenger.
Reason : Insulin is a peptide hormone which can easily pass through cell membrane to interact with intracellular receptors in cell cytoplasm.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Insulin is a peptide hormone produced in the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas. Insulin interacts with membrane bound receptors and does not enter target cell but generates second messenger. Insulin receptors for most cells are less than 100 . Insulin binds to receptors located on plasma membrane to form hormone receptor complex which induces release of GDP from G protein which activates adenyl cyclase that in turn catalysis the formation of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) from ATP. The hormone is called first messenger and cAMP is termed as second messenger.

questions.solution: The secretion of the posterior lobe of pituitary is known as pituitrin and it contains two hormones. (i) Oxytocin or pitocin. (ii) Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or vasopressin. The posterior lobe of the pituitary gland does not secrete any hormone. Its hormones are secreted in the hypothalamus. Oxytocin (OT) promotes contraction of the uterine muscle and contraction of the myoepithelial cells of the lactating breast, squeezing milk into the large ducts behind the nipple. In late pregnancy the uterus becomes very sensitive to oxytocin. The amount secreted is increased just before and during labour and by sucking of the baby. Because of its role, oxytocin is called "birth hormone" and "milk ejecting hormone."

questions.solution: Placenta is the intimate connection between the fetus and uterine wall of the mother to exchange the materials. The outer surface of the chorion in humans develops a number of finger like projections, known as chorionic villi, which grow into the tissue of the uterus. These villi, penetrate the tissues of the uterine wall in which they are embedded, make up the organ known as the placenta by means of which the developing embryo obtains nutrients and oxygen and gets rid of carbon dioxide and metabolic wastes. Because the chorion takes part in the formation of placenta, the human placenta is called the chorionic placenta. It consists of fetal part, the chorion and a maternal part the decidua basalis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In cockroach
options: ejaculatory duct opens in phallic gland
vas deferens opens in phallic gland
phallic gland opens in left phallomere.
questions.solution: Phallic gland is a large elongated saclike structure which lies beneath the utricular gland and the ejaculatory duct. It tapers posteriorly and terminates into a duct near the male gonophore on the left phallomere. The secretion of phallic gland forms the outermost layer of the spermatophore.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following holds true for blood circulation in earthworm?
options: Oxygen is not transported by blood.
questions.solution: Blood vascular system of earthworm is of closed type as blood flows in closed blood vessels. Oxygen carrying respiratory pigment, haemoglobin is present in the plasma due to which the colour of plasma is red. Only one type of blood corpuscles, leucocytes are present in the blood of earthworm.
